description: Workflow Builder page -- the core authoring environment where users create, edit, and manage multi-phase AI automation workflows. Users can generate complete workflows from natural language prompts using AI, manually build workflows step-by-step across four phases (setup, verification, agentic, completion), manage a sidebar library of saved workflows, configure individual steps, run workflows directly, and export/import workflows as JSON. The default landing state shows the AI Generate panel with a prompt textarea and spec source section; selecting a workflow reveals the full phase editor with Run, Save, and Export controls.

groups.name: AI Workflow Generation
groups.description: The default landing experience centers on AI-powered workflow generation. When no workflow is selected, users see a prominent panel inviting them to describe what they want to automate in natural language. The system generates a complete multi-phase workflow from the description, optionally incorporating page specs for spec-driven verification, attached contexts for additional AI guidance, and generation templates for common patterns. Users can select the AI provider and model, configure advanced options like max iterations and discovery mode, and choose between Generate (create and review) or Generate & Run (create and immediately execute). The prompt text persists across sessions via localStorage so users can refine their description over time.

assertions.description: Users can enter a natural language description of the automation they want in a prominent text area, which serves as the primary input for AI workflow generation
Users can trigger AI workflow generation from their prompt, producing a complete multi-phase workflow that appears in the editor for review and refinement before execution
Users can generate and immediately execute a workflow in a single action, bypassing the manual review step for rapid iteration on automation tasks
Users can attach page specification files as a source for the AI to generate spec-driven verification steps, enabling automated UI validation based on existing page specs
Users can select the AI provider (Claude CLI, Claude API, Gemini CLI, Gemini API) and model to use for workflow generation, allowing control over generation quality and cost

groups.name: Workflow Sidebar Library
groups.description: The sidebar provides a persistent library of all saved workflows, allowing users to browse, search, create, duplicate, and delete workflows. It serves as the primary navigation mechanism for switching between workflows in the editor. Users can search by name to quickly locate a specific workflow, create new blank workflows, and manage their collection. The sidebar shows workflow names and metadata, and selecting a workflow loads it into the main editor panel. The sidebar can be toggled to maximize editor space.

assertions.description: Users can search saved workflows by name to quickly find a specific workflow without scrolling through the full list
Users can create a new blank workflow from the sidebar, which opens an empty editor with all four phases ready for manual step configuration
Users can click a workflow in the sidebar to load it into the main editor, replacing the AI generation panel with the full phase editor showing the workflow's steps and configuration
Users can collapse and expand the sidebar panel to maximize the editor workspace when the workflow library is not needed

groups.name: Multi-Phase Workflow Editor
groups.description: When a workflow is loaded, the main content area displays a structured editor organized into four execution phases: Setup (environment preparation commands), Verification (checks and tests run between AI iterations), Agentic (AI prompts and instructions that drive the automation), and Completion (cleanup and finalization steps). Each phase section supports adding, removing, reordering, and configuring individual steps with type-specific editors. Users can expand and collapse phase sections to focus on the phase they are editing. The phase structure ensures workflows follow a predictable execution pattern.

assertions.description: Users can define setup steps that run before AI execution to prepare the environment -- installing dependencies, starting services, or configuring the workspace
Users can define verification steps that run between AI iterations to validate progress -- including shell commands, check groups, playwright tests, and UI bridge assertions
Users can define agentic steps containing AI prompts and instructions that drive the core automation work, with the AI iterating until verification passes or max iterations are reached
Users can define completion steps that run after the AI finishes to clean up resources, generate reports, or finalize the automation output
Users can add new steps to any phase using an add button that presents available step types (command, prompt, check, check group, playwright test, etc.) appropriate for that phase

groups.name: Workflow Execution and Persistence
groups.description: The editor toolbar provides essential workflow lifecycle controls. Users can run the currently loaded workflow directly from the editor, save changes back to the library, export the workflow as a JSON file for sharing or backup, and import previously exported workflows. The Run button launches workflow execution and transitions the view to show execution progress. Save persists all step configurations, settings, and metadata. Export produces a portable JSON file that can be imported into another runner instance.

assertions.description: Users can execute the currently loaded workflow directly from the editor, launching the multi-phase execution pipeline and transitioning to the execution monitoring view
Users can save the current workflow state including all steps, settings, and metadata back to the persistent library for future use
Users can export the workflow as a portable JSON file for sharing with others or backing up workflow definitions

groups.name: Workflow Settings and Configuration
groups.description: Each workflow has configurable settings that control execution behavior. Users can name and describe the workflow, select the AI provider and model, set max iterations for the verification loop, enable or disable reflection mode for self-improving workflows, configure timeouts, enable health checks for target services, and toggle various execution options. Settings are organized into logical sections and use toggle switches, dropdowns, and number inputs appropriate for each setting type. The settings panel is accessible via a gear icon when a workflow is loaded.

assertions.description: Users can set a descriptive name and description for the workflow to identify it in the library and understand its purpose at a glance
Users can configure the maximum number of verification-agentic loop iterations, controlling how many times the AI retries before the workflow stops
Users can enable reflection mode which allows the workflow to analyze its own failures and generate improved strategies for subsequent iterations
Users can open the settings panel via a gear icon button to access all workflow configuration options without cluttering the main editor view

groups.name: HTN Planning Configuration
groups.description: The HTN (Hierarchical Task Network) Planning section within workflow settings allows users to enable structured plan-based fixes that run before the AI agentic session. When enabled, the verification loop attempts to find and execute a deterministic plan using a state machine and method library before falling back to AI. The section has three controls: an enable toggle (off by default), a UI Bridge URL text input (for connecting to the target app's UI Bridge during plan execution), and a state machine path input (for specifying a custom state machine JSON file; defaults to the bundled runner state machine). The URL and path inputs are conditionally visible — they only appear when HTN is enabled.

assertions.description: The HTN Planning section is visible in the workflow settings panel with a section header labeled 'HTN Planning' and an info tooltip icon that explains what HTN planning does
assertions.precondition: Settings panel is open (gear icon clicked)

assertions.description: Hovering the info icon next to the HTN Planning header shows a tooltip explaining: 'Hierarchical Task Network planning uses a state machine to attempt structured fixes before the AI agentic session. Useful when the application has well-defined UI states and transitions.'
A toggle switch labeled 'Enable HTN Planning' is present in the HTN section. It defaults to off (unchecked). The toggle uses a blue background when active and zinc/gray when inactive.
The HTN Planning toggle defaults to off (unchecked) for new workflows, since HTN requires app-specific state machines to be useful
assertions.precondition: Settings panel is open and workflow has not been modified

assertions.description: When HTN Planning is disabled (toggle off), the UI Bridge URL and State Machine Path text inputs are not visible — only the enable toggle is shown in the HTN section
assertions.precondition: Settings panel is open and HTN toggle is off

assertions.description: When HTN Planning is enabled (toggle on), two additional text inputs appear below the toggle: 'UI Bridge URL' with placeholder 'http://localhost:1420' and 'State Machine Path' with placeholder 'Default: data/runner_state_machine.json'. Both use monospace font for config values.

The UI Bridge URL input is a text field with placeholder 'http://localhost:1420' and helper text 'UI Bridge endpoint for querying element state. Leave empty for plan-only mode.' Users can enter the URL of the target application's UI Bridge for live GUI interaction during HTN execution.
assertions.precondition: Settings panel is open and HTN toggle is on

assertions.description: The State Machine Path input is a text field with placeholder 'Default: data/runner_state_machine.json' and helper text 'Path to a state machine JSON file. Defaults to the bundled runner state machine.' When left empty, the runner automatically uses its bundled state machine with 14 states covering all runner pages and common dialogs.
assertions.precondition: Settings panel is open and HTN toggle is on

assertions.description: HTN settings (enabled, URL, path) are persisted when the workflow is saved. After saving and reloading a workflow with HTN enabled and a custom URL, the toggle should still be on and the URL should be populated with the saved value.
assertions.precondition: A workflow with HTN enabled has been saved and reloaded

assertions.description: The HTN Planning section uses a semi-transparent dark background (bg-zinc-800/50), rounded corners, and consistent spacing matching other advanced settings sections like Health Check. Labels are text-sm font-medium text-zinc-400, helper text is text-xs text-zinc-500, and inputs use bg-zinc-800 with border-zinc-700 borders and blue focus rings.

groups.name: Step Configuration and Library Integration
groups.description: Individual workflow steps can be configured with type-specific settings. Command steps have shell commands, working directories, and timeouts. Prompt steps have AI instruction text and context attachments. Check and check group steps reference items from the check library. Playwright test steps reference saved test scripts. Users can also pick steps from library pickers that show saved prompts, shell commands, checks, check groups, tests, and MCP server tools. The step configuration panel opens when a step is selected, showing all relevant fields for that step type. This tight integration with the asset library enables reuse across workflows.

assertions.description: Users can add multiple step types to workflows including shell commands, AI prompts, verification checks, check groups, playwright tests, and MCP tool invocations, each with type-appropriate configuration

target.label: Phase section with add step capability

assertions.description: Users can browse and select from their saved asset library when adding steps, pulling in reusable prompts, commands, checks, and tests rather than configuring from scratch
Users can configure step-specific settings inline within the editor, including command text, working directory, timeout values, prompt content, and assertion parameters

states.name: AI Generate Panel — Default Landing
states.description: The default state when no workflow is loaded. Shows the AI generation panel with a prompt textarea, spec source section, context attachments, provider/model selectors, and Generate / Generate & Run buttons. The phase editor is not visible.

transitions.name: Generate workflow or create manually
transitions.description: User clicks Generate, Generate & Run, or Create Manually to produce a workflow with steps, transitioning to the phase editor

transitions.name: Select existing workflow from sidebar
transitions.description: User clicks a saved workflow in the sidebar library, loading it into the editor

states.name: Phase Editor — Multi-Phase Workflow Editing
states.description: The main editing state when a workflow with steps is loaded. Shows the four phase sections (Setup, Verification, Agentic, Completion), the stage selector tab bar, toolbar with Save/Run/Export, and the sidebar library. Settings and Constraints panels are hidden.

transitions.name: Open settings panel
transitions.description: User clicks the gear icon button in the toolbar to reveal the settings panel above the phase editor

transitions.name: Open constraints panel
transitions.description: User clicks the shield icon button in the toolbar to reveal the constraints panel

transitions.name: Select a step to configure
transitions.description: User clicks on a step within any phase section, opening the step configuration side panel on the right

transitions.name: Run workflow
transitions.description: User clicks the Run button to execute the workflow, showing the execution status bar

transitions.name: Reset to new (empty) workflow
transitions.description: User clicks New in the sidebar to clear the editor back to the AI generate panel

states.name: Settings Panel — Workflow Configuration
states.description: The settings panel is expanded above the phase editor, showing workflow name, description, provider/model selection, max iterations, reflection toggle, and other execution options. The phase editor remains visible beneath. Constraints panel is hidden (mutually exclusive).

transitions.name: Close settings panel
transitions.description: User clicks the gear icon again to collapse the settings panel, returning to the plain phase editor

transitions.name: Switch to constraints panel
transitions.description: User clicks the shield icon to close settings and open constraints (mutually exclusive panels)

states.name: Constraints Panel — Execution Constraints
states.description: The constraints panel is expanded, showing constraint configuration for the workflow. Settings panel is hidden (mutually exclusive). The phase editor remains visible beneath.

transitions.name: Close constraints panel
transitions.description: User clicks the shield icon again to collapse the constraints panel

transitions.name: Switch to settings panel
transitions.description: User clicks the gear icon to close constraints and open settings (mutually exclusive panels)

states.name: Step Configuration Side Panel
states.description: A step is selected and the right-side configuration panel (w-96) is visible, showing type-specific settings for the selected step including command text, working directory, timeout, prompt content, or assertion parameters depending on step type.

transitions.name: Close step config panel
transitions.description: User closes the step configuration panel by clicking the close button or deselecting the step, returning to the full-width phase editor

states.name: Executing — Workflow Running
states.description: The workflow is currently being executed. A blue status bar is shown below the toolbar indicating the running workflow name with a spinner. The Run button is replaced by a Stop button. The phase editor remains visible underneath.

transitions.name: Execution completes or is stopped
transitions.description: The workflow finishes execution (success or failure) or the user clicks Stop, returning to the normal phase editor with a success or error banner
